mathematical_findings: For PSD D, every spectral value t is nonnegative. The pointwise scalar b(1-indicator(t<=b))<=t holds for every real b, including b<=0, and the closed cutoff includes equality t=b.

Functional-calculus order transfers the pointwise bound to b(I-P_b)<=D. Finite matrix spectrum makes every scalar function continuous on that spectrum; no global continuity of the threshold indicator is assumed or asserted.
Taking the quadratic form at a unit v yields b(1-Re<v,P_bv>)<=Re<v,Dv>. Division requires precisely b>0 and gives the stated first-moment mass bound.
The spectral projection is the actual real functional calculus of D, with the characteristic function of (-infinity,b]; no projection or expectation certificate is supplied as a hypothesis.
The signatures and blueprint state generic first-moment consequences, not the full actual replica count/gap/symmetry construction from comparator:defect-mass.
